texts: good. both trigger actions become conditions of one fireable rule sharing the Keeper and the feather batch, 'the feathers' and 'the lantern' refer back correctly, and 'around' and 'against' are kept as stated.
good. the 'whenever' phrasing lands on the same fireable rule, with both the grinding and the spreading required before the shielding follows.
good. it becomes a blanket denial covering every wraith and every warded lantern, and — correctly — no particular warded lantern is asserted to exist.
good. 'fresh' and 'ground' both restrict the rule rather than being dropped, so it fires only for fresh ground feathers.
good. the mirror image of the previous sentence, with 'stale' and 'ground' both kept as conditions, so warding is denied only for stale ground feathers.
